raw_segments.text: The present author is by no means a philosopher.
He has not comprehended the system, whether it exists, whether it is finished.
He already has enough to do for his weak head with the thought of what a prodigious head
every man in our age must have, since every man has such a prodigious thought.
Even were one able to transpose the entire content of faith into the form of the concept,
it would not follow that one had comprehended faith, comprehended how one came into it,
or how it came into one.
The present author is by no means a philosopher.
He is, Poetus et Elegantor, a supplementary scribe who neither writes the system nor promises
of the system, who neither subscribes himself to the system nor signs himself over to it.
He writes because for him it is a luxury, which gains in agreeableness and self-evidence
the fewer there are who buy and read what he writes.
He readily foresees his fate in an age that has drawn a line through passion in order
to serve science, an age in which an author who would have readers must take care so
to write that his book may conveniently be leafed through during the after-dinner nap,
and take care to model his outward bearing after that polite gardener's apprentice in
the addressy vison who, had in hand and with good recommendations from the place where
he last served, recommends himself to a most honored public.
He foresees his fate to be wholly ignored.
He divines the more dreadful prospect that the zealous criticism will several times stand
him at the school bench.
He shudders at the still more dreadful prospect that some industrious registrar, some paragraph
glutton, who, to save science, is always ready to do unto the writings of others what crop.
To save taste, magnanimously did unto the destruction of the human race, will cut him
up into section section, and do it with the same inflexibility as that man who, to serve
the science of punctuation, divided his discourse by counting the words.
So that fifty words made one full stop, and thirty-five a semicolon.
I prostrate myself in deepest humility before every systematic peeping tom.
This is not the system.
It has not the slightest thing to do with the system.
I call down every blessing upon the system and upon the Danish shareholders in this omnibus.
For a tower, indeed, it will scarcely become.
I wish them all and every one of them luck and benediction.
